column10: Host to the annual Walleye Festival, Waterworks Park is nestled along the picturesque shores of Lake Erie. The well-maintained pathways meander through vibrant flower beds and towering trees, making it an ideal spot for nature lovers and photographers alike. Whether you're interested in birdwatching, jogging, or simply unwinding by the water, the park caters to all kinds of outdoor enthusiasts. Families will appreciate the ample space for children to play and explore, making it a perfect destination for a day out. The covered picnic area can be reserved for groups.

When the church was demolished in 2011 the City of Port Clinton installed the garden and named it in her honor. There is a plaque in the garden that pays homage to the church's historical significance. The garden is managed by the Friends of Port Clinton Parks and is open to all members of the community. The pathways in the garden were made wide enough to accommodate anyone who might have mobility challenges. There are 25 all organic raised beds that can be rented out, with a one-time fee of $25 for each bed.

column10: Originally gifted to the City of Port Clinton in 1933, Veterans Memorial Park stands as a tribute to those who give the most they have to offer. The park is dedicated to the memory of the 37th Tank Company of the Port Clinton National Guard, who served as Company C from the 192nd Tank Battalion during World War II. The men of Company C were taken prisoner while defending the Bataan Peninsula in 1942 and were held until their liberation in 1945. Only 10 men of the original 32 sent to the Bataan Peninsula survived. There are visual testimonials of military service throughout the park. A restored World War II M5 anti-tank gun guards the south entrance and a M-42 'Duster' tank guards the north entrance. The Fallen Soldier Battlefield Cross adorns one side of the park while an Eternal Flame lights the other.

column10: Great Egret Marsh Preserve consists of more than 150 acres of marsh and surrounding upland in Ottawa County, across the road from East Harbor State Park. The preserve's marshes are part of the West Harbor Basin, a long, narrow pool of Lake Erie backwater that geologists believe was once the channel of the Portage River. Created in 2013 with help from a Clean Ohio Conservation Fund grant, the preserve contributes to TNC's goal to protect and restore an additional 10,000 acres of coastal habitat along Lake Erie.

column10: An iconic reminder of the Great Lakes' rich natural heritage, the 68-acre Bay Point property along the Lake Erie shore has been acquired by Western Reserve Land Conservancy. Known locally as the 'Sandbar,' the Ottawa County property consists of a narrow peninsula that extends south from the Marblehead Peninsula into Sandusky Bay. The northern portion of the property is more stable and contains mature trees along with extensive forested wetlands. The southern portion is seemingly under constant change by shifting sands and wave activity, comprising beaches, sandbars, small sand dunes, as well as coastal wetlands.
